### Handoff note (end every delivery with this)

```
HANDOFF · <page, site or fix> · route <full|light> · <date>
handoff: <the line scripts/handoff.mjs printed, pasted: VALIDATED | CONDITIONAL | NOT VALIDATED | REFERENCE · hash · …>

### Measured
gate.mjs     <the full stamp line it printed: critique: … · gate: … · rules: … · gate/n · id · skipped …>
             <the X lines and the J line: journey: nav0 mobile0 forms0 loading0 errors0 session0, each failing state named>
originality  <originality.mjs pairs against earlier builds, per axis; not run → Not verified>
contrast     <contrast.mjs ratios for any colour you changed>
cost         <cost.mjs: tokens in/out, wall clock, tool calls, retries; benchmark runs only>

### Judged
self (opinion)   Chose: <archetype + mutation, signature, type, palette, tier>, because <reason from the brief>
self (opinion)   Rejected: <the obvious option> because <why>
self (opinion)   C <n> · R <n> (from my own Restraint Gate record) · AI-default scan <n>/25 by eye · craft checklist by eye: <failed items or "none">
judge (opinion)  <independent judge scores and notes, named, or "none">
self (opinion)   Try next: <one command, e.g. /bolder on the hero, or /motomate the product chapter>

### Not verified
<each check that did not run or could not decide, with the reason: "gate.mjs: not verified — no browser"; axes marked ?;
 journey checks that printed n/a and why; O with no earlier build; real devices, screen readers, copy accuracy>
handoff      <every exception handoff.mjs listed, one per line; a CONDITIONAL note lists all of them>
prototype    <every browser-only, simulated or unavailable operation handoff.mjs listed: the prototype's honest edge>
forms        Form states are checked by intercepting requests in the browser. No real server exists for /api/* endpoints. When the template ships, replace the mock endpoints with a real server.
<[NEEDS COPY] / [NEEDS ASSET] items: placeholders, nothing claimed about them>
```

The status is computed, never typed: `node scripts/handoff.mjs <site> --report <the note>` rejects a note whose `handoff:` line differs from the record, or which claims more than its status (`gates/handoff.md`). The light route writes the same three sections; for a fix, **Measured** has the gate's before and after lines side by side.

<!-- file: gates/handoff.md -->

## Development checks and handoff validation (v3.0.2)

Two kinds of checking, never confused. **Development checks** are fast and partial: they guide the build. **Handoff validation** is the full gate on the approved files: it decides what the handoff may claim. The handoff status is computed by `scripts/handoff.mjs` from what actually ran. It is pasted, never typed.

Why this exists: in the v3.0.1 benchmark, three of the four builders never ran the journey check (axis J), because the full gate was too heavy for their machines. Two of them said so. The third wrote "All 3 core journeys connect without broken paths" in `GATE.md`, with J never run. Nothing in the toolchain could tell the two kinds of note apart. Now it can: `handoff.mjs --report GATE.md` rejects the second one (`fixtures/handoff/b2b-overclaim-GATE.md`, `tests/gate/handoff.test.mjs`).

### The two tiers

| Tier | Commands | When | What it may claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Development checks** | `node scripts/completeness.mjs <site>` (X, seconds) · `node scripts/gate.mjs --rules <page>` (C S P K, seconds) · `node scripts/gate.mjs --journey <site>` (J only, a few minutes) · `node scripts/gate.mjs <one page>` while fixing it | any time during the build, as often as useful | nothing beyond its own line. A `--journey` pass is not a handoff; a `--rules` pass says nothing about journeys |
| **Handoff validation** | `node scripts/gate.mjs <site>` (every axis, J included, on the approved files), then `node scripts/handoff.mjs <site> --report GATE.md` | once, at Checkpoint 6, after the author approved the design, and again after any later edit | exactly the status `handoff.mjs` printed |

Run J as a development check early, as soon as two routes and one form exist (`--journey`, a few minutes). Most J failures (an overflowing header, a form that claims to send) are cheaper to fix then than at the end.

### The record and the status

Every gate run writes `<project>/.motomation/gate-record.json`: the mode (`full`, `journey`, `rules`, or `not-verified` when the run could not finish), the date, the machine, each target's result, the journey summary, and a hash of the site's files (stamps pasted into pages, `GATE.md`, `CRITIQUE.md` and other notes do not count as changes). A URL target has no files to hash: pass `--record <project folder>`. `--no-record` writes nothing (fixtures, experiments).

`node scripts/handoff.mjs <project>` reads the record and prints one line, then the reasons:

| Status | When | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATED` | a full gate run passed on the current files; J ran, passed, and left nothing unverified | 0 |
| `CONDITIONAL` | the full run passed, but J listed something it could not verify: a form behind a state a fresh browser lacks (an empty cart, a signed-out account), a form that rejected the filled values, a submit kept disabled while empty, a Scope route no link reaches, a route beyond the page cap | 3 |
| `NOT VALIDATED` | no full run; only development checks ran; the full run was on older files; the run failed; the run ended "not verified" (no browser, a constrained machine, a timeout); J was not measured | 1 |
| `REFERENCE` | a design reference gated with `--reference`: J does not apply | 0 |

A build with an unverified critical journey never gets `VALIDATED`. Walking an exception by hand is useful and goes in `GATE.md` under **Judged** (`self (opinion): walked the checkout by hand at 375px, …`), but the status stays `CONDITIONAL`: a hand walk is a judgement, not a measurement.

**Prototype boundaries** are listed separately, not as exceptions: forms that save only in the browser, simulations that say so, features marked unavailable (`thinking/product-contract.md` → Forms and operations). They do not block `VALIDATED`, and the handoff names them, so nobody mistakes a labelled demo for a working flow.

### The handoff note

`GATE.md` and the handoff note (`gates/delivery-gate.md` → Handoff note) start with the `handoff:` line `handoff.mjs` printed, pasted. Then:

- `node scripts/handoff.mjs <site> --report GATE.md` checks the note against the record. It rejects a note with no `handoff:` line, a status other than the computed one, a line pasted before the last change (a different hash), and, unless the status is `VALIDATED`, any unqualified claim such as "fully validated", "all journeys connect", "production-ready" or "no known issues". A `CONDITIONAL` note must list every exception. Exit 2 means the note contradicts the record. Fix the note (or the site), not the checker.
- A note may never say a check passed when it did not run. "Rule-only results; the journey check did not run (CPU limit)" is honest and accepted. "Product integrity: all 3 core journeys connect" with J never run is rejected.

### When the full gate cannot run

On a constrained machine (2 CPUs, a short tool timeout) the full gate may not finish. Then:

1. Run the development checks that do finish: `completeness.mjs`, `gate.mjs --rules`, and `gate.mjs --journey` (J alone takes minutes, not the full gate's 2–5 minutes per page per width). Fix what they find.
2. Try the full gate once with the default budget and a tool timeout above it. `gate.mjs` already retries a failed scan in the light footprint (`--light`).
3. If it still cannot finish, the run ends `not verified — <reason>`, and the record says so. `handoff.mjs` prints `NOT VALIDATED` with that reason. Paste it. The handoff says the build was not validated, and why, and lists the development checks that did run under **Measured** with their own names (`gate.mjs --journey: journey: nav0 …`). Never as the full gate.
4. Validation is then a separate step on a machine that can run it (CI, a larger sandbox): `gate.mjs <site>` there, then `handoff.mjs`. That is the honest path, not a weaker gate.

<!-- file: gates/rules.md -->

## Rules (design input)

Read before Step 1. Design inside these. `scripts/gate.mjs` measures them after the build; `gates/delivery-gate.md` verifies them.

### Contrast (gate `c`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| Body text | ≥ 4.5:1 against the pixels behind it |
| Large text (≥ 24px, or ≥ 18.66px bold) | ≥ 3:1 |
| Widths measured | 375, 390, 768, 1440px |
| Sample judged | the 10th-percentile background sample, not the median |
| Scroll positions | every 0.7 viewport; every 0.15 viewport in pinned zones; 0/25/50/75/100% of page and zone |
| Scroll-sequence steps | AA in the active state and in every inactive (dimmed) state |
| Dimmed text | measured as rendered: text × opacity + background × (1 − opacity) |
| Forced colors | rendered ink ≥ 3:1 against its box |
| Accent *(heuristic, H-one-accent)* | ≤ 5% of each screen; colour that encodes data, status or a colour-rich brand system is not accent |

### Overflow and long words (gate `o`, `w`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| Horizontal scroll | none at 375, 390, 768, 1440px |
| Element past viewport or parent | ≤ 1px, unless a clipping ancestor |
| Display text at 375px (h1–h3, any text ≥ 32px) | fits its box, stays in the viewport, no word broken across lines |
| One word split across elements | never |
| Reflow at 320px | no horizontal scroll |

### Hierarchy (critique `H`, SEO `S`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| `h1` | exactly one per page |
| Heading levels | no skipped level |
| Largest text on the first 375px screen *(heuristic, H-focal)* | one on storytelling screens; dense product screens follow a reading order instead |
| Body size | ≥ 16px |
| Measure | ≤ 75ch |

### Reduced motion (gate `rm`, `q`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| `prefers-reduced-motion` path | every animation has one |
| Text visible in full motion | visible under reduced motion |
| Still page | no pixels change |
| Pinned zones | none pinned under reduced motion |
| Fallback | a designed still: unpinned plates, every step visible |
| Values | no value later corrected (no "0" before a count-up) |

### Motion quality and budgets (gate `q`, critique `M`, `V`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| Pinned zone progression | median change between 8 samples > 0.5% of pixels |
| Smoothness, p95 rAF interval | ≤ 20 ms at 1440; ≤ 25 ms at 375 with CPU ×4 (unconstrained machine only) |
| Pinned sections | ≤ 2 |
| WebGL canvases | ≤ 1 |
| JS gzipped, Tier 1 | ≤ 30KB beyond the framework |
| JS gzipped, Tier 2 | ≤ 80KB |
| JS gzipped, Tier 3 | ≤ 140KB |
| JS gzipped, Tier 4–5 (or tier unknown) | ≤ 250KB |
| Section entrance patterns *(heuristic, H-entrance-variety; critique V)* | on narrative pages, avoid repeating one entrance on every section; on product pages consistency is correct |
| UI feedback (press, hover, focus, toggle, tooltip) | ≤ <!--rule:ui_feedback_max_ms-->250ms<!--/rule--> |
| Entrances | no `scale(0)`, no ease-in |
| Animated properties | `transform`, `opacity`; never `top`, `left`, `width`, `height` |
| Off-screen loops and canvases | paused |
| Scroll | never hijacked: keyboard, anchors and screen readers keep working |

### Accessibility (gate `a`, `k`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| `img` | has `alt`; decorative uses `alt=""` |
| Focusable elements | have an accessible name |
| Focus ring | changes ≥ 1% of the pixels around the element |
| Touch targets at 375 | ≥ 24×24px (inline links exempt); < 44px warns |
| 200% zoom (720×450 CSS viewport) | no text clipped, no control off screen or covered |
| Keyboard | no trap; every tabbable element reachable |
| Clickable elements | real `a`/`button`, never a clickable `div` |
| Landmarks and skip link | present |

### Content and defaults (Delivery Gate Part 2)

Rows marked *(heuristic)* are advisory defaults (authority level 6, `principles/heuristics.md`): a reason in the plan replaces them. The other rows are hard.

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| Display face *(heuristic, H-banned-display)* | not <!--rule:banned_display_fonts-->Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Poppins, Montserrat, Arial, Helvetica or the system UI stack<!--/rule--> |
| Caution faces *(heuristic)* | <!--rule:caution_fonts-->Playfair Display and Space Grotesk<!--/rule--> only with a stated reason |
| Display faces *(heuristic)* | one (two only for a contrast concept) |
| Accent colours *(heuristic)* | one brand accent; data, status and brand-system colours don't count |
| Signature moves *(heuristic)* | at most one; none is valid |
| Placeholder copy | none: no lorem ipsum, "Acme", "John Doe", "Product 1", no TODO or process notes in customer copy (`scripts/realism.mjs`) |
| Statistics, logos, testimonials, awards | real and sourced, `[NEEDS COPY]`, or labelled illustrative (`scripts/realism.mjs`) |
| Links, domains, pages | only those the brief supplies or the build creates; no `href="#"` controls that go nowhere |
| Capability claims | a control is never presented as working when it isn't; demo-only interfaces are labelled (`thinking/product-contract.md`) |
| Emoji as icons or bullets | none |
| Gradients, blobs, glass, bento, three-icon feature row *(heuristic)* | only with a concept reason |
| Code | no TODOs, `// ...rest`, `markers: true`, stray `console.log` |

### Copy (gate `rules: C`, `craft/copy.md`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| copy-04 | no em dash in visible copy, `alt`, title or description |
| copy-09 | no aphorism formula ("It's not X, it's Y") |
| copy-11 | no warm-up opener |
| copy-15 | no two-beat antithesis ("Not just X, but Y") |
| copy-17 | no vague CTA label ("Learn more", "Submit", "Click here") |
| copy-06 | paragraphs ≤ 4 lines (warns) |
| copy-16 | no unsourced "trusted by N" claim (warns) |

### SEO (gate `rules: S`, `craft/seo.md`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| seo-03 | no `noindex` on public pages |
| seo-04 | exactly one canonical; error pages (status ≥ 400, or 404/500/error/not-found pages) are exempt, a canonical on one warns |
| seo-05 | title ≤ 60 characters, unique |
| seo-06 | description ≤ 160 characters, unique |
| seo-07 | one `h1` |
| seo-08 | no skipped heading level |
| seo-10 | JSON-LD parses; schema where eligible (warns when missing) |
| seo-11 | ≥ 3 internal links to other pages (all of them when `sitemap.xml` lists fewer) |
| seo-16 | no mixed content |
| seo-17 | slugs lowercase, hyphenated, no IDs or query strings |
| seo-18 | `og:image` present, 1200 × 630 |
| seo-01, seo-02, seo-12 | sitemap, robots.txt, zero broken links (site level) |

### Performance (gate `rules: P`, `craft/performance.md`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| perf-01 | raster images AVIF or WebP |
| perf-02 | below-the-fold images `loading="lazy"` |
| perf-03 | LCP image not lazy |
| perf-04 | JS gzipped within the tier budget |
| perf-11 | no empty inline scripts |
| perf-12 | no render-blocking head scripts |
| perf-07 | scripts > 2KB minified (warns) |
| Hero image | ≤ 200KB |
| `img`/`video` | `width` and `height` or an `aspect-ratio` box |
| Fonts | ≤ 1 preloaded file, `font-display: swap` |
| Core Web Vitals | LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1 (never claimed unmeasured) |

### Micro-states (gate `micro-states`, warns)

| Thing | Ships |
|---|---|
| Button | default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading |
| Form | default, validation error, submit loading, success, server error |
| List | empty, loading, error, filled (data lists carry `data-entity`) |
| Image | loading, loaded, error |
| Async action | idle, pending, success, error |

### Completeness (gate `X`, `scripts/completeness.mjs`)

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| Product contract | written in `DESIGN.md` under `## Product contract` and approved (Checkpoint 2) before any concept; required whenever a delivery mode is stated |
| Scope | derived in Step 1 from the contract, written in `DESIGN.md` under `Scope`; never from a fixed list |
| Journeys | each core journey a `journey` row whose evidence is its route sequence (`/ → /shop → /cart`); every route in it exists |
| Capability levels | optional `Level` column: interface, interaction, persisted, backend, integration; a design exploration or functional frontend never claims backend or integration |
| Deferrals | a backend or integration deferral names the interface that still ships (`…; interface: /checkout`), and that route exists |
| Content realism | `scripts/realism.mjs`: no leaked process notes, template fixture names, repeated fixtures (> 25% duplicate names, one price for every record) or dead `#` links |
| Requested and required items | every one present (route found, or evidence file and text found) |
| Excused items | "not required for this brief, reason: <why>"; a reason is required |
| Marks | requested, required, optional, or excused; anything else fails |
| Template shape (`templates/TEMPLATE.md`, by delivery mode; production template shown, and the default) | `README.md` (with "All data in data/ is demo. Replace with real data before launch."), `DESIGN.md`, `MOTION.md`, `SCHEMA.md`, `DATA.md`, `CRITIQUE.md`, `GATE.md`, `LICENSE`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `.env.example` covering every env var the code reads, `middleware.ts`, the build's `data/` folder with its `schema.json` and every entry labelled demo, a `dev` script; each unless excused |
| Research and readiness | with a delivery mode stated: `DESIGN.md` has `## Product contract`, `## Type research` and `## Research record` (or v2 `## References`); `README.md` calls the build production-ready only in a production template with no asset left to replace |
| Media (`craft/media.md`) | `MEDIA.md` in every mode, never excused: an inventory (or "no external media assets were used"), source and licence status per row, placeholders and unknown licences marked for replacement, every local media file and every `placeholder-…` file and `PLACEHOLDER:` comment listed, `README.md` pointing to it while anything needs replacing; without a Scope section (maintenance), the same media check whenever `MEDIA.md` exists, and placeholders always |
| Middleware, comments, component headers | checked as warnings |

### Security (gate `rules: K`, `craft/security.md`)

Every [M] rule of `craft/security.md`. "warns" = heuristic, printed, never counted.

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| sec-01 [M] | admin routes require auth and carry `noindex` |
| sec-03 [M] | row-level security on every user-data table where the database supports it |
| sec-06 [M] | auth cookies `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite` (gate); no auth token in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` (gate warns) |
| sec-07 [M] | no secret-shaped string in served HTML or JS (gate) |
| sec-08 [M] | `.env`, `.env.*` in `.gitignore`; only `.env.example` committed (gate warns, local targets) |
| sec-09 [M] | no `console.*` or log line that prints a token, key, password, session id or email (gate warns) |
| sec-11 [M] | every form input validated on the server with a schema |
| sec-12 [M] | no URL- or user-controlled value written with `innerHTML`/`outerHTML`/`document.write` (gate) |
| sec-13 [M] | uploads checked by real MIME type against an allow-list and by size |
| sec-15 [M] | rate limits on auth, contact and every mutation |
| sec-16 [M] | no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` in production (gate) |
| sec-17 [M] | no debug mode, development build or public source map in production (gate warns) |
| sec-20 [M] | role, user id, tenant and price never taken from the client |
| sec-h1 | `Content-Security-Policy` sent (gate; header or meta; meta only over HTTP warns) |
| sec-h2 | `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` sent as a header (gate) |
| sec-h3 | `Referrer-Policy` sent, header or meta (gate) |

<!-- file: commands/critique-format.md -->

## Critique Format

Use this exact structure for `/critique` and for the critique step inside `/overdrive`.

```
CRITIQUE · <page or component> · <date>

### Measured
gate.mjs        H <n> · M <n> · V <n> · Q <n> · A <n> · S <n>, with the traces it printed (the critique: segment without C and R)
                gate: c o w rm a n q k · rules: C S P K · the X lines · journey: nav mobile forms loading errors session
contrast.mjs    <failures with the ratio and the pair, e.g. 3.1:1 #8a857a on #f3efe6>
performance     <numbers a tool printed: JS gzipped, LCP, CLS; none printed → Not verified>
originality.mjs <scores against earlier builds, if it ran>

### Judged
self (opinion)  C <n> · R <n> (counted by gate.mjs from my own Restraint Gate record: self-reported)
self (opinion)  Verdict: <one sentence: the single biggest reason it does or doesn't work>
self (opinion)  Top 3 problems (most important first)
                1. <problem> — where: <section/file:line> — why it matters: <effect on the user> — evidence: <"see Measured: …" or "by eye">
                   Fix: <specific change>
                2. …
                3. …
self (opinion)  AI-default scan <n>/25 failed, by eye: <list gate numbers>
self (opinion)  Restraint Gate, per questioned element: <element> — Q1 hierarchy/feedback/storytelling <pass|fail> · Q2 brief
                needs it to feel like itself <pass|fail> → <kept|cut>   (cut only if both fail; principles/restraint.md)
self (opinion)  Motion: <passes / animations failing the four questions>
self (opinion)  Choreography <n>/5 against MOTION.md's timing sheet: <drift, grammar, camera, rhythm, reduced motion>
                (motion/choreography.md §5; "no timing sheet" on Tier 3–5 is a failure)
self (opinion)  Keyboard and focus, by hand: <issues found by tabbing, or "none found">
judge (opinion) <an independent judge, named, with its scores and notes, or "none">
self (opinion)  Keep: <the 1–3 things that are working and must survive the revision>
self (opinion)  Next command: <e.g. /mutate hero, /type, /quieter>

### Not verified
<every check that did not run or could not decide, with the reason: "not verified — no browser", axes marked ?, n/a journey
 checks, performance not measured, real devices, screen readers>
```

### Rules

- Be specific: name the element, the value and the fix. "Increase hero display size from 64px to clamp(4rem, 12vw, 14rem)", not "make it bolder".
- Every problem links to a user effect (confusion, slowness, distrust, inaccessibility, forgettability).
- Never invent measurements. A number goes under **Measured** only if a tool printed it; name the tool. Performance you didn't measure goes under **Not verified**, with the reason.
- Three sections, no mixing (`gates/delivery-gate.md`, "Every report"). Every **Judged** line says `(opinion)` and who judged (`self` or a named `judge`). A problem may cite measured evidence (`see Measured: contrast`) but does not restate its numbers. A check done by hand (tabbing, reading copy) is judged, not measured: no tool observed it.
- Always include **Keep**. Critique protects what works.
- Never recommend cutting an element for failing Q1 alone. If it passes Q2 (the brief needs it to feel like itself), it stays; name the brief's reason. Recommend a cut only when it fails both.

<!-- file: commands/overview.md -->

## Commands

Type a command at the start of a message. Commands combine with flags. Without a command, the skill runs `/build` when the request is to create something, and `/critique` when it's to review.

### Flags (work with every command)

| Flag | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--route` | full · light | Force the route (`SKILL.md` "Routes"). Without it the agent picks: light for narrow maintenance inside an established design, full for any new design work (even one page), and says which in its first line. Light never skips research for new design work |
| `--tier` | 1–5 | Force a motion tier |
| `--energy` `--rhythm` `--motion` | 1–3 | Set a dial (see `principles/dials.md`) |
| `--style` | a file in `styles/` | Apply a visual language |
| `--stack` | next · react · vanilla · astro | Target framework. Without it: detect from the project, else choose and show it in the plan (Step 0 in `thinking/sequence.md`) |
| `--seed` | any number | Repeatable collision draws |
| `--review` | — | Every build stops at the six checkpoints (`thinking/sequence.md`); `--review` keeps them even when the brief pre-approves every checkpoint |

---

### Create

#### `/shape [brief]`
**What:** turns a brief into a design direction without code: brief inference, the Thinking Sequence, dials, and a `DESIGN.md` + `SCHEMA.md` + `MOTION.md`.
**When:** at the very start, or when the client must approve a direction first.
**Output:** preview block + `DESIGN.md` + `SCHEMA.md` + `MOTION.md` (from `templates/`; `SCHEMA.md` is written with `DESIGN.md`).

#### `/build [brief] [--route=full|light]`
**What:** the full flow, from brief to finished, gated code, in the delivery mode the request asks for (design exploration, functional frontend or production template; `templates/TEMPLATE.md`). Full route order: stack → product contract and scope (approved before any concept) → design research → directions and synthesis → memory → restraint → build plan → build → review → gate. `--route=light` (narrow maintenance inside an established design) skips the contract, research and direction work, and still runs the whole Delivery Gate.
**When:** you want a new page or site, any size (full), or a fix inside an existing design (light).
**Output:** preview block → complete code → Delivery Gate scores → handoff note.

#### `/invent [topic]`
**What:** runs the collision engine (`scripts/collide.mjs --n 3 --spread`; `--count N` for more) and proposes **three different concepts**, each with tension, concept, type mode (HOUSE STYLE or SERVICE STYLE, with the reason from the brief), archetype + mutation, collision and signature.
**Guarantees (enforced by the script, reported in its "Diversity (measured)" block):** the three draws never share an archetype or a signature seed; mutations and collision worlds don't repeat either while their pools last (12 mutations, 23 archetypes, 22 signature seeds). When `--count` asks for more than a pool holds, the script says which pool ran out and from which draw repeats start; it never overlaps silently. Copy that block into the output. Without a shell, draw by hand and state that uniqueness was checked by eye.
**When:** you're stuck, or the first idea feels familiar.
**Output:** three concept cards plus the measured diversity line. The draws are fuel, not a menu: each card derives its tension, concept and specifics from the brief, using the drawn archetype, mutation and collision as constraints. Each card keeps the product contract intact when one exists (`principles/authority.md`); a card that needs a contract change says so. Choose a card and continue with `/build`.

#### `/signature [section]`
**What:** invents one signature move for the site or a section, bent from `signatures/` to the concept.
**When:** the page works but nobody will remember it.
**Output:** the move in recipe format (idea, why, build, detail, off-switch, prompt) and its implementation.

#### `/motomate [section]`
**What:** turns a section into a Tier 5 scroll-film: storyboard in `MOTION.md`, technique choice (DOM, image sequence, video, WebGL), asset pipeline, code and fallbacks.
**When:** a product, place or story should play like a film as you scroll.
**Output:** storyboard table + ffmpeg commands (if needed) + code + static fallback.

#### `/animate [target] --tier=n`
**What:** adds motion to existing UI at the given tier, following the four questions.
**When:** the design is done but static.
**Output:** a motion plan (what moves, why, tokens) + code.

#### `/type [target]`
**What:** a typography pass: face choice with reasons, fluid scale, tracking, wrapping, numerals, variable-axis opportunities.
**When:** the page feels generic, and the type is usually why.

---

### Tune

#### `/bolder [target]`
Raises ENERGY by one step: bigger type jumps, stronger contrast, a braver accent moment, one more grid break. Keeps the concept.

#### `/quieter [target]`
Lowers ENERGY and/or MOTION by one step: more air, fewer moving parts, softer accent, slower reveals.

#### `/distill [target]`
Removes until only the essential remains. Runs the Restraint Gate hard: at most one signature, one accent, fewer sections; never fewer contract items.

#### `/mutate [target]`
Keeps the content and concept but changes the **structure**: a different archetype or mutation, drawn with `collide.mjs`. Use it when the layout feels like a template.

#### `/overdrive [target]`
A generate → critique → improve loop, up to 3 rounds. Each round scores the six critique axes and fixes the lowest one. Stops when every axis is 4 or more. Use it for flagship pages.

---

### Evaluate

#### `/critique [target or URL]`
A design review in the format of `commands/critique-format.md`: scores, the three most important problems, and fixes in priority order. Doesn't change code unless asked.

#### `/audit [target]`
A technical gate: accessibility, performance, reduced motion, mobile matrix, SEO and the AI-default scan. Returns pass/fail per item with file and line references.

#### `/study [reference URL or screenshot]`
Extracts the **design DNA** of a reference **without copying it**, and writes it into `DESIGN.md` as a "Studied direction" in five sections: type, palette, layout, motion, signature. It ends with what to take (decisions) and what to leave (anything that would make a copy). Agent-driven: the agent opens the URL or reads the screenshot, and no script fetches anything. Measured values are marked as measured, and missing evidence as `not observed`. Full input, output and rules: `commands/study.md`.

---

### Ship

#### `/polish [target]`
The final pass: spacing rhythm, alignment, typographic details (quotes, dashes, numerals), focus states, hover/press states, empty and error states, loading, favicon and OG image, the stamp comment and the memory log.

---

### Meta

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/dials` | Shows the current dials and tier, or sets them: `/dials energy=3 motion=2` |
| `/help` | Lists commands with one-line descriptions and suggests the next step |
| `/version` | Prints the installed version from `VERSION` |
| `/check-update` | Compares the installed version with the latest on GitHub (see `commands/update.md`) |
| `/update-skill` | Explains how to update: `npx skills update asfakulsiam-motomation-design` |

### Typical sequences

- New site: `/shape` → approve → `/build` → `/critique` → `/polish`
- Stuck on ideas: `/invent` → pick → `/build --review`
- Existing site feels generic: `/critique` → `/mutate` → `/type` → `/signature`
- Product launch: `/shape --energy=3 --rhythm=3` → `/motomate hero-product` → `/audit`


---

<!-- file: commands/study.md -->

## `/study [url | screenshot]`

**What:** reads an existing page (a URL the agent opens, or a screenshot the user attaches) and writes its **design direction** into `DESIGN.md`, in five sections: type, palette, layout, motion, signature. It studies how the page makes its decisions so a new design can learn from it. It doesn't clone the page.

**When:**
- The client says "like this site".
- You inherit a page and need its system written down before `/redesign`.
- A reference needs to be checked against the anti-sameness rules before you borrow from it.

### Input

- **URL:** the agent opens it with whatever browsing or browser tool it has. `/study` itself fetches nothing and runs no script against the URL. If the agent can't open pages, ask for a screenshot.
- **Screenshot:** one or more images. Desktop and 375px views give the best read. Without a 375px view, mark the responsive part as `not observed`.
- **Optional:** `--section <name>` to study one part only (hero, nav, a pinned chapter).

### Output

A `DESIGN.md` built from `templates/DESIGN.md`, with a **Studied direction** block at the top:

```markdown
### Studied direction
- Source: <url or "screenshot, <date>">, studied <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Read by: <how: live page with computed styles | screenshot only>

#### Type
Families (display / text / mono) and how you know (computed style, or "looks like" for screenshots), scale ratio, weights, tracking, case, the one typographic decision that carries the page.

#### Palette
Ground, surface, ink, muted, accent as hex values (sampled, not guessed). Contrast of ink/ground and accent/ground, from `scripts/contrast.mjs` where a shell exists. Where the accent is used and where it isn't.

#### Layout
Grid and margins, section rhythm, nav pattern, the closest archetype from `structures/archetypes.md`, and what breaks the grid on purpose.

#### Motion
Motion tier (1–5) and the evidence for it (transitions, scroll-linked effects, pinning, WebGL), the easing and duration feel, and what happens under reduced motion (`not observed` if you couldn't test it).

#### Signature
The one moment people remember, described as a concept in this skill's vocabulary (`references/effects-vocabulary.md`). Say whether it serves the page's idea or decorates it.

#### What to take / what to leave
Two short lists. "Take" holds decisions, never assets. "Leave" names what would make a new design read as a copy.
```

### Rules

1. **Direction, not assets.** Don't copy logos, photographs, illustrations, copy, code or font files. Fonts are named, not downloaded. Commercial faces get an alternative from `data/fonts.csv`.
2. **Measure what you can, label what you can't.** Live page: read computed styles and sample colours. Screenshot: say "looks like" for fonts, sample hex values from the pixels, and mark motion as `not observed`.
3. **Every section is filled.** Write `not observed` when evidence is missing. Never guess silently.
4. **Study, then diverge.** A studied direction is a starting point. Before `/build`, run the Thinking Sequence's anti-sameness step against it, so the new page shares at most two of: layout family, type pairing, palette, signature.
5. **Credit the source** in the Studied direction block.
6. **No automatic fetching.** `/study` is agent-driven: the agent decides to open the page and records what it saw. No script in this skill requests the URL.

<!-- file: commands/update.md -->

## Updating

### Check the installed version
Read `VERSION` in the skill folder. `/version` prints it.

### Check for a newer version
Compare with the latest release:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design/main/skills/asfakulsiam-motomation-design/VERSION
```
If the remote version is higher, tell the user and show the update command. Don't update automatically.

### Update
```bash
npx skills update asfakulsiam-motomation-design        # project install
npx skills update asfakulsiam-motomation-design -g     # global install
```
Claude Code plugin users: `/plugin marketplace update asfakulsiam-motomation-design`.
Chat tools (ChatGPT, Grok, Google AI Studio, v0, Lovable): download the new `dist/motomation-design.md` and replace the old file in your project or instructions.

After updating, read `CHANGELOG.md` in the repository for what changed.

## Adapter: Astro

> **Dependencies (`craft/stack.md`, checked 2026-10-16):** `gsap` 3.15.0 and `lenis` 1.3.27 are approved: active, not deprecated, licence free for commercial use (GSAP Standard no-charge licence; Lenis MIT). Re-check npm and the repo (deprecation, last release, licence) at build time.

- Content-first and zero-JS by default, so it's great for editorial sites and SEO.
- Put motion in a `<script>` inside the component (bundled and deduplicated), or in a framework island (`client:visible`) for React components.
- Cross-document View Transitions: `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` in global CSS, or Astro's `<ClientRouter />`. With the client router, re-initialise GSAP on `astro:page-load` and kill triggers on `astro:before-swap`.
- Fonts with Astro's font API or `@fontsource-variable/*`.


---

<!-- file: adapters/next.md -->

## Adapter: Next.js (App Router)

> **Dependencies (`craft/stack.md`, checked 2026-10-16):** `gsap` 3.15.0 and `lenis` 1.3.27 are approved: active, not deprecated, licence free for commercial use (GSAP Standard no-charge licence; Lenis MIT). Re-check npm and the repo (deprecation, last release, licence) at build time.

```bash
npm i gsap @gsap/react lenis
```

- Motion components are client components (`"use client"`). Keep pages and layouts as server components, and pass content down as props, so text is server-rendered for SEO.
- Fonts: `next/font/google` or `next/font/local`, exposed as CSS variables:
  ```ts
  import { Fraunces, Inter_Tight } from "next/font/google";
  const display = Fraunces({ subsets: ["latin"], axes: ["SOFT", "WONK", "opsz"], variable: "--font-display" });
  ```
- Register GSAP plugins once in a client module (`lib/gsap.ts`) and import from there.
- Smooth scroll: a client `<SmoothScroll>` provider in `app/layout.tsx` using `ReactLenis` with `autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`. See `examples/providers/smooth-scroll.tsx`.
- Route changes: call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after the new page mounts; `useGSAP` reverts the old page's triggers on unmount.
- Images: `next/image` with `sizes` and `priority` on the LCP image. Image sequences live in `/public/film/…` and are drawn to a canvas (no `next/image`).
- Three.js: `dynamic(() => import("./Scene"), { ssr: false })`.
- Stamp: the build minifies CSS and drops ordinary comments, so write the stamp (`SKILL.md` → Output rules) at the top of `app/globals.css` as `/*! motomation · … */` and check it survives in `.next/static/css/` or `out/_next/static/css/`.
- Metadata: export `metadata` / `generateMetadata` per route, plus `app/opengraph-image.tsx`, `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts` and `public/llms.txt`.

## Platform Notes: Using This Skill Everywhere

| Platform | How to use the skill | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Cline, Roo, Kiro, OpenCode, Goose, Junie, Zed, Amp** and other skills-compatible agents | `npx skills add asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design` | The agent loads `SKILL.md` and reads the other files on demand. Scripts run in the terminal |
| **Claude Code (plugin)** | `/plugin marketplace add asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design`, then `/plugin install asfakulsiam-motomation-design@asfakulsiam-motomation-design` | Same skill, managed as a plugin |
| **Claude.ai / Claude Desktop** | Upload the skill folder as a zip under Settings → Capabilities → Skills (where available), or attach `dist/motomation-design.md` to a Project | Without a shell, it uses the CSV data directly |
| **ChatGPT** | Add `dist/motomation-design.md` to a Project's files or a custom GPT's knowledge, and add "Follow motomation-design.md for every web design task" to the instructions | Use the single-file prompts in `signatures/` |
| **Grok, Google AI Studio, Gemini app** | Paste `dist/motomation-design.md` into the system instructions, or attach it to the conversation or project | Ask for one `index.html` using `adapters/vanilla.md` |
| **v0, Lovable, Bolt, Replit Agent** | Add the content of `dist/motomation-design.md` to the project's knowledge, rules or custom instructions | Name the stack these tools use (Next.js / React + Tailwind) |

### Without a shell

When scripts can't run:
1. **Collisions:** use the seed method in `invention/mad-artist.md` with the CSVs in `data/`.
2. **Search:** read the relevant CSV and choose deliberately. Never take the first row.
3. **Memory:** ask the user to keep the stamp comment. Check stamps in the code they paste back.
4. **Contrast:** calculate WCAG contrast manually, or ask the user to verify with any contrast checker.

## Adapter: React + Vite

> **Dependencies (`craft/stack.md`, checked 2026-10-16):** `gsap` 3.15.0 and `lenis` 1.3.27 are approved: active, not deprecated, licence free for commercial use (GSAP Standard no-charge licence; Lenis MIT). Re-check npm and the repo (deprecation, last release, licence) at build time.

```bash
npm create vite@latest site -- --template react-ts && cd site && npm i gsap @gsap/react lenis
```

- Use `useGSAP(() => …, { scope })` for every animation; it handles cleanup on unmount and in Strict Mode.
- Smooth scroll provider at the root, as in the Next adapter (no `"use client"` needed).
- Pre-render marketing pages (e.g. `vite-plugin-ssg`, or move to Astro/Next) if SEO matters. A client-only SPA hides content from crawlers until JS runs.
- Self-host fonts with `@fontsource-variable/<family>` packages where available.
- Code-split heavy scenes with `React.lazy(() => import("./Scene"))`.

## Adapter: Plain HTML / CSS / JS

> **Dependencies (`craft/stack.md`, checked 2026-10-16):** `gsap` 3.15.0 and `lenis` 1.3.27 are approved: active, not deprecated, licence free for commercial use (GSAP Standard no-charge licence; Lenis MIT). Re-check npm and the repo (deprecation, last release, licence) at build time.

The most portable route: works in any host, and in chat tools that can only produce one file.

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/SplitText.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1/dist/lenis.min.js" defer></script>
```

- Pin versions in production (e.g. `gsap@3.15.0`) and self-host if you can.
- Add `class="js"` to `<html>` in an inline script, so CSS can hide static fallbacks only when JS runs.
- Wrap all motion in `gsap.matchMedia()` exactly as in the framework examples.
- A complete single-file reference lives in `examples/html/motomation-film.html`.

## Effects Vocabulary

A shared language for effects, so a designer and an agent mean the same thing. Each entry is a **concept**, described in this skill's own words, with the tier it needs and when it earns its place. The **In this skill** column points to this skill's own component (`examples/components/`, catalogue in `examples/components/README.md`), signature or example. Everything referenced here was written for this skill.

Find before build (see `SKILL.md`, step 6): for a standard effect, check the project's own components first, then this table and the component library, before writing it from scratch. The signature move is never swapped for a ready-made effect.

### Text effects

| Concept | What it does | Tier | Earns its place when | In this skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Line rise | Lines slide up from behind masks | 2 | Default editorial reveal | `examples/animation/line-curtain.tsx` |
| Blur focus | Words sharpen from blur into focus | 2 | The concept is about clarity or focus | `examples/components/type/blur-focus.tsx` |
| Decode | Characters resolve from random glyphs | 2 | Technical, secret or data-led brands; short labels only | signature `decode` · `examples/components/type/decode.tsx` |
| Proximity weight | Weight/width follows cursor distance | 2 | Type-led identities; one word only | signature `proximity-weight` in `signatures/type-signatures.md` · `examples/typography/proximity-weight.tsx` |
| Pressure type | Letters stretch or compress toward the cursor | 2 | Playful, elastic brands | `examples/components/type/pressure-type.tsx` |
| Scroll float | Letters bob into place as they scroll in | 2 | Buoyant, light-hearted display lines | `examples/components/type/scroll-float.tsx` |
| Ink fill | Words fill from muted to ink while reading | 2 | Manifestos, about statements | signature `ink-fill` · `examples/components/type/ink-fill.tsx` |
| Velocity type | Text skews or widens with scroll speed | 2 | Sport, speed, launches | signature `velocity-skew` · `examples/components/scroll/velocity-marquee.tsx` · `examples/components/type/width-sprint.tsx` |
| Split-flap | Characters flip like a departure board | 2 | Schedules, menus, travel | `examples/components/type/split-flap.tsx` |
| Curved text | Text runs along a circle or path | 1–2 | Badges, stamps, seals | `examples/components/type/curved-text.tsx` |
| Text gradient sweep | A highlight runs across the text | 1 | A single key word, rarely | concept only (CSS `background-clip: text` with a moving gradient; one word) |
| Type film | A headline choreographed across a pinned chapter | 5 | Motomation hooks | `motion/tier-5-motomation.md` · `examples/html/motomation-film.html` |
| Neighbour moves | Each letter of a name has its own small move on hover, so the word feels like a cast | 2 | Light-hearted names and logotypes of 3–12 letters | `examples/components/type/neighbour-moves.tsx` |
| Letter relay | The hero name shrinks and travels into the header letter by letter as the first screen scrolls away | 2 | The name is the identity (portfolios, personal brands) | `examples/components/type/letter-relay.tsx` |

<!-- file: references/gsap-lenis.md -->

## GSAP + Lenis Quick Reference

> **Dependencies (`craft/stack.md`, checked 2026-10-16):** `gsap` 3.15.0 and `lenis` 1.3.27 are approved: active, not deprecated, licence free for commercial use (GSAP Standard no-charge licence; Lenis MIT). Re-check npm and the repo (deprecation, last release, licence) at build time.

### Imports
```js
import gsap from "gsap";
import { ScrollTrigger } from "gsap/ScrollTrigger";
import { SplitText } from "gsap/SplitText";
import { Flip } from "gsap/Flip";
import { useGSAP } from "@gsap/react";
import Lenis from "lenis";
gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip, useGSAP);
```

### ScrollTrigger options you'll use most
| Option | Typical |
|---|---|
| `start` / `end` | `"top 80%"`, `"top top"`, `"+=300%"`, `() => "+=" + el.offsetWidth` |
| `scrub` | `true` (exact) or `0.5–1.5` (weight) |
| `pin` | `true`; add `anticipatePin: 1` for fast scrollers |
| `once` | `true` for reveals that shouldn't replay |
| `toggleActions` | `"play none none reverse"` for non-scrubbed reveals |
| `invalidateOnRefresh` | `true` when values are functions of layout |
| `containerAnimation` | animate items inside a horizontal pinned track |

### Lifecycle
- React: `useGSAP` with `{ scope }`; everything is reverted on unmount.
- Vanilla: `const ctx = gsap.context(() => {...}, root); ctx.revert();`
- Responsive and reduced motion: `gsap.matchMedia()`, which reverts automatically when queries change.
- After fonts/images: `document.fonts.ready.then(() => ScrollTrigger.refresh())`.

### Lenis
```js
const lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, lerp: 0.1 });    // smaller lerp = smoother and slower
lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update);
gsap.ticker.add((t) => lenis.raf(t * 1000));
gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
// anchor links: lenis.scrollTo("#section", { offset: -80 })
// stop during modals: lenis.stop(); lenis.start();
```
Lenis respects `prefers-reduced-motion` by default and keeps native touch scrolling unless you set `syncTouch: true` (don't, for most sites). Add `data-lenis-prevent` to scrollable inner panels.

### Debugging
- `markers: true` during development only.
- `ScrollTrigger.getAll()` to list triggers; `ScrollTrigger.killAll()` in hot-reload edge cases.
- If pinned sections jump: check for CSS `transform` on ancestors, and fonts loading after measurement.

## Inspiration and Resource Libraries

Use these to **study**, not to copy. Run `/study <url>` to extract principles. The wider, status-checked source lists for Steps 1–2 are in `references/sources/` (protocol: `craft/research.md`).

| Need | Go to |
|---|---|
| Award-level sites to study | awwwards.com, thefwa.com, cssdesignawards.com, godly.website, siteinspire.com |
| Motion and scroll references | gsap.com/showcase, codepen.io (search "ScrollTrigger"), lenis.darkroom.engineering |
| Effect components | this skill's own library: `examples/components/` (catalogue in its README, live demos in `examples/gallery/index.html`) |
| Small interaction ideas with prompts | github.com/miguelclavel/interaction-recipes |
| Type | fonts.google.com, fontshare.com, pangrampangram.com, typewolf.com, fontsinuse.com |
| Colour | coolors.co, oklch.com, huemint.com, realtimecolors.com |
| 3D and shaders | threejs.org/examples, shadertoy.com, thebookofshaders.com |
| Illustrated motion | lottiefiles.com, rive.app/community |
| Accessibility checks | webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker, wave.webaim.org |
| Performance checks | pagespeed.web.dev, web.dev/articles/vitals |

### Rules for using references
1. Collect three references from **outside** the category (a hotel brief studies a bookshop, a film title and a museum).
2. Extract principles: what is the structure, the type logic, the motion language?
3. Never copy a layout, illustration or code wholesale. Check the license before using any asset or code.

## Award-site teardowns

Written analyses of award-winning sites: structure, type, motion beats, and what made each one memorable. **Principles only, no code**: nothing here is copied from the sites, and nothing should be. Read a teardown for the reasoning, then design your own page with the skill's own method (`thinking/`, `invention/`).

Facts (awards, dates, what the page does) are linked to their source in each file. Where a source only records a behaviour, the teardown says only that.

| Site | Award | Category · style | Teardown |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lando Norris | Awwwards Site of the Year 2025 | personal brand · kinetic type | `references/teardowns/lando-norris.md` |
| Messenger | Awwwards Developer Site of the Year 2025 | studio · flat | `references/teardowns/messenger.md` |
| Scout Motors | Awwwards E-commerce of the Year 2025 | e-commerce · editorial | `references/teardowns/scout-motors.md` |
| Igloo Inc | Awwwards Site of the Year 2024 | portfolio · glassmorphism | `references/teardowns/igloo-inc.md` |
| Lusion v3 | Awwwards Site of the Year 2023 | studio · minimal | `references/teardowns/lusion-v3.md` |
| Prometheus Fuels | Awwwards Site of the Year 2021 | education · product launch | `references/teardowns/prometheus-fuels.md` |
| Siena Film Foundation | Awwwards Site of the Month, Mar 2025 | organisation · dark luxe | `references/teardowns/siena-film-foundation.md` |
| Cartier Watches & Wonders 2025 | Awwwards Site of the Month, Aug 2025 | event · dark luxe | `references/teardowns/cartier-watches-wonders-2025.md` |
| Terminal Industries | Awwwards Site of the Month, Sep 2025 | SaaS · Swiss | `references/teardowns/terminal-industries.md` |
| Bruno Simon | Awwwards Site of the Month, Jan 2026 | portfolio · flat | `references/teardowns/bruno-simon.md` |
| Active Theory | Sites of the Day (earlier versions) | studio | `references/teardowns/active-theory.md` |

### What they share

1. **The concept comes from the subject's own name or object** (an igloo in ice, a messenger delivering, a ticket for a film foundation).
2. **One reveal shape, one material, one art direction**, held across the page.
3. **The first screen holds the claim and its proof.**
4. **Motion has a meaning** (a transition that explains, a pointer that scrubs film), never decoration.

### Where this skill differs

These sites often put text inside a canvas, gate content behind an intro, or run dozens of scroll-scrubbed channels. This skill does not: text stays in the DOM, every page passes the delivery gate (`gates/delivery-gate.md`), and motion is budgeted by the dials. Take the principle; leave the excess.

<!-- file: references/teardowns/active-theory.md -->

## Teardown: Active Theory (studio site)

**Award:** earlier versions of the site were Awwwards Sites of the Day; an award for the current version is unverified ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)). The studio made Prometheus Fuels, Site of the Year 2021 ([Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com/annual-awards-2021/site-of-the-year)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/studio.md` · archetype `stage`

### Structure
One continuous WebGL scene is the site. A full-screen intro boots into navigation; the nav lists what the studio makes (games, multiplayer, XR, installations, websites) next to a sound toggle and a track player.

### What made it memorable
Sound is part of the identity: the audio toggle is a deliberate gate, and the player names the song.

### Principles to take
- **The nav is the capability list.** A studio's menu can say what it does in five words.
- **Sound is opt-in and named.** If a site has music, show the control and the track, and start muted.
- **The portfolio can be the demo.** For a studio that sells real-time 3D, the site itself is a case study.

### What not to take
Headings that are empty in the DOM because the words live on a canvas. Screen readers and search see nothing. Keep the words in HTML.

<!-- file: references/teardowns/bruno-simon.md -->

## Teardown: Bruno Simon (portfolio)

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Month, Jan 2026 ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md); [Futurists' 2026 list](https://futurists.in/10-best-award-winning-websites-of-2026/)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/portfolio.md` · `styles/flat.md` · archetype `field-guide`

### Structure
A drivable 3D world: the visitor steers a small vehicle around a landscape where the work and the contact points are places to drive to ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).

### What made it memorable
The portfolio proves the skill it sells. Nobody forgets driving into a project.

### Principles to take
- **Proof over description.** A creative developer's portfolio can be its own best project; a designer's can be its best layout.
- **A playground has rules.** A world needs edges, a map and a way out; give the visitor all three.
- **Offer the fast path.** Keep a plain list of projects and contact for people who came to hire, not to play.

### What not to take
A world where finding the contact details is the game.

<!-- file: references/teardowns/cartier-watches-wonders-2025.md -->

## Teardown: Cartier Watches & Wonders 2025 (Immersive Garden)

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Day 18 Aug 2025 and Site of the Month Aug 2025; CSSDA Website of the Day 16 Jul 2025 ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md); [WebGPU showcase](https://www.webgpu.com/showcase/cartier-watches-and-wonders-immersive-garden/)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/event.md` · `styles/dark-luxe.md` · archetype `room`

### Structure
Six 3D rooms that the visitor moves between by scrolling, for a trade-fair launch, with a Web Audio score.

### Motion beats
1. Scroll is travel from room to room: one collection or idea per room.
2. A score accompanies the walk.

### What made it memorable
A fair stand translated into a place: the visitor tours the booth the way they would on the fair floor, at home.

### Principles to take
- **One room, one idea.** Six rooms means six things to remember, no more. This is the room archetype at full scale.
- **Luxury is pace.** Long, slow transitions and few elements read as expensive; quick cuts read as retail.
- **Translate the physical event.** For an event site, ask what walking the venue feels like, then build that walk.

### What not to take
Six WebGL rooms for a single-night event. Scale the number of rooms to the content: `categories/event.md` asks for the date, the line-up and the tickets first.

<!-- file: references/teardowns/igloo-inc.md -->

## Teardown: Igloo Inc (abeto with Bureaux)

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Year 2024 and Developer Site of the Year 2024 ([Awwwards announcement](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/awwwards_we-are-thrilled-to-announce-that-the-winners-activity-7307431367728861187-ED07); [Awwwards case study](https://www.awwwards.com/igloo-inc-case-study.html)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/portfolio.md` · `styles/glassmorphism.md` · archetype `gallery-wall`

### Structure
A three-section landing page for a parent company: an outdoor opening scene, its portfolio companies each frozen inside a block of ice, and a links section where particles form a different model for each external link ([case study](https://www.awwwards.com/igloo-inc-case-study.html)).

### Type
The interface itself is drawn in WebGL so that glitches and text scrambles are cheap; type behaves like the material around it.

### Motion beats
1. An intro gives the outdoor scene a "tech" turn.
2. Scrolling moves between ice blocks; each project's block has its own form.
3. Transitions use chromatic aberration on selected materials.
4. In the links section, particles swirl into shapes, change colour with speed and glow; music and sound effects follow the particles.

### What made it memorable
The name is the concept: an igloo company shows its companies in ice. Every visual decision follows from that one word.

### Principles to take
- **Take the concept from the name.** Before choosing a style, ask what the brand's name already is (`thinking/`, collision method in `invention/mad-artist.md`).
- **One material, many objects.** Ice for every project gives variety inside one system.
- **Sound follows motion, never leads it.** If you add audio, tie it to something the visitor caused, and keep it off until asked.
- **Performance is part of the brief.** The team designed for smooth scrolling on low-end devices from the start.

### What not to take
UI text rendered only in WebGL. In this skill, text stays in the DOM and passes the gate's contrast and forced-colors checks.


---

<!-- file: references/teardowns/lando-norris.md -->

## Teardown: Lando Norris (OFF+BRAND)

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Year 2025 and Site of the Year Users' Choice 2025 ([Digidop's summary of the 2025 annual awards](https://www.digidop.com/blog/5-web-design-trends-2025); [observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/personal-brand.md` · `styles/kinetic-type.md` · archetype `stage`

### Structure
A long single page of about twelve sections: a full-bleed portrait on a cream ground, an "on track" horizontal gallery, an on-track/off-track split, a helmets gallery, the championship honour, partners, and a designed footer that returns to the portrait.

### Type
Two-line name locked to a corner, set in one variable grotesk; nav labels roll between two copies of the word. The name does the work a logo would.

### Motion beats
1. An intro assembles a brand mark while assets load, then hands to the hero through an elliptical reveal.
2. Headline lines rise through masks without fading.
3. Images reveal through the same ellipse and scale inside it, so every image arrives the same way.
4. One shared ease and one shared duration for nav and menu motion.

### What made it memorable
The ellipse is one shape used everywhere (intro, images, footer), so the page feels authored by one hand. The lime accent is the driver's colour and appears only where action is (store, call to action, footer strip). The loading state is a pun on the name.

### Principles to take
- **One reveal shape per page.** Pick the shape from the subject (a visor, a lens, a door) and use it for every entrance. See the Aperture signature in `signatures/scroll-signatures.md`.
- **The accent marks action.** If the brand colour is loud, spend it only on things you can press.
- **Close on the opening image, changed.** The footer recontextualises the hero; the visitor feels the page end.
- **A personal brand is a person, not a CV.** Portrait first, facts as chapters.

### What not to take
Dozens of simultaneous scroll-scrubbed channels. Motion budget in this skill is set by the dials (`principles/dials.md`), not by what a studio with a racing budget shipped.


---

<!-- file: references/teardowns/lusion-v3.md -->

## Teardown: Lusion v3

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Year 2023 and Developer Site of the Year 2023; CSSDA Website of the Year 2023; FWA of the Year 2023 ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/studio.md` · `styles/minimal.md` · archetype `gallery-wall`

### Structure
A statement headline over a live 3D scene, a short manifesto, a reel of project cards tagged by discipline, a link to all projects, and a contact-first footer with a real street address.

### Type
One grotesk throughout. The headline is a full sentence saying exactly what the studio does; small uppercase microcopy carries the scroll cue.

### Motion beats
1. The claim and the 3D proof share the first screen.
2. Project cards split their discipline tags letter by letter on hover or scroll while the 3D object changes.
3. A custom smooth scroll with two dominant easing curves used across the site.

### What made it memorable
It is a light-key site in a genre that defaults to black. The headline is plain language, so the 3D does the showing and the words do the telling.

### Principles to take
- **Claim and proof on the same screen.** A studio that says "3D storytelling" shows 3D in the first viewport, not on page four.
- **Plain sentence, rich medium.** The richer the motion, the plainer the headline. See `craft/copy.md`.
- **Two eases for a whole site.** A small easing vocabulary is a house style (`motion/tokens.md`).
- **Address in the footer.** A real place builds more trust than another animation.

### What not to take
A canvas as the only carrier of content. Keep project titles and links in the DOM.


---

<!-- file: references/teardowns/messenger.md -->

## Teardown: Messenger (abeto)

**Award:** Awwwards Developer Site of the Year 2025 ([Digidop's summary of the 2025 annual awards](https://www.digidop.com/blog/5-web-design-trends-2025); [observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/studio.md` · `styles/flat.md` · archetype `stage`

### Structure
No sections and no routes: one small planet rendered in the browser, where the visitor makes deliveries. The world is the page.

### Motion beats
1. Camera and scene motion replace scrolling.
2. The visitor drives the loop: pick up, travel, deliver.
3. Physics, light and animation run continuously; the site is replayable.

### What made it memorable
Agency. The visitor is not shown a showcase, they do a job inside it, and the job (delivering messages) is the name.

### Principles to take
- **A verb beats a gallery.** If the brand's name is a verb or a role, let the visitor perform it.
- **Small world, finished edges.** A tiny planet can be complete; a big one can't. Scope the experience to what can be polished.
- **Experiences are a separate deliverable.** This skill's Tier 4 and 5 (`motion/tier-4-max.md`, `motion/tier-5-motomation.md`) stop at scroll-driven pages; a game-like world needs its own accessible alternative page.

### What not to take
Navigation that exists only in a 3D world. Any site in this skill keeps a plain-HTML route to every piece of content.


---

<!-- file: references/teardowns/prometheus-fuels.md -->

## Teardown: Prometheus Fuels (Active Theory)

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Year 2021 ([Awwwards Annual Awards 2021](https://www.awwwards.com/annual-awards-2021/site-of-the-year)); FWA of the Year 2021 ([FWA announcement](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-mountford_after-9-years-in-the-biz-we-finally-get-activity-6889646337080614912-OZ4h)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/education.md` · `categories/product-launch.md` · archetype `timeline`

### Structure
A stylised interactive story about making fuel from the air ([Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com/sites/prometheus-fuels)). The art lead describes turning a technical process into a retro-futurist road-trip sequence of dramatic scenes, vehicles, mountains and planets, with storyboards set first ([Rafael Dante](https://rafaeldante.com/project/prometheus)).

### Motion beats
1. Each scene is one step of the process, told as a stop on the road trip.
2. Scroll moves the camera through the story like chapters of a film.
3. New chapters were released later ("The Need for Speed"), so the site grew like a series ([Prometheus Fuels' founder](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gmcgurgan_awwwards-thefwa-fuelfromtheair-activity-6915450420928675840-l7tP)).

### What made it memorable
A jury member called it "a literal showcase of the art of Storytelling and Art Direction" that "felt like a movie" ([Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com/annual-awards-2021/site-of-the-year)). The science was not simplified into icons; it was turned into a journey with a destination.

### Principles to take
- **Explain a process as a journey.** Each step becomes a place. This is the timeline archetype with a camera.
- **Storyboard before you build.** The art direction and script came first; this skill's Tier 5 timing sheet (`motion/choreography.md`) is the same discipline.
- **Chapters can ship later.** A story site can be episodic; plan the chapter slots.
- **One art direction, held.** Retro-futurism across every scene is what makes it feel like one film.

### What not to take
Scene length that hides the facts. A visitor who wants the numbers needs them in text, one tap away.


---

<!-- file: references/teardowns/scout-motors.md -->

## Teardown: Scout Motors (Locomotive)

**Award:** Awwwards E-commerce of the Year 2025 ([Awwwards announcement](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/awwwards_the-e-commerce-of-the-year-award-goes-to-activity-7436441178805518336-25xm)); Site of the Day, Mar 2025 ([Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com/sites/scout-motors)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/ecommerce.md` · `styles/editorial.md` · archetype `catalogue`

### Structure
A commerce platform for a revived vehicle brand, "born from an American legend, retooled for a new era" ([Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com/sites/scout-motors)): brand storytelling and product exploration sit inside the actual purchase and configuration path ([Metabole's review](https://metabole.studio/en/blog/immersive-website-examples)).

### What made it memorable
The agency describes the brief as carrying a heritage forward under tight deadlines with shared standards ([Locomotive](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/locomotive-mtl_scout-motors-inc-just-won-e-commerce-of-activity-7434609007316770817-HHF7)). The award went to a store, not a campaign page: the storytelling survives into the funnel.

### Principles to take
- **Story inside the funnel, not before it.** Motion that explains the product belongs on the product and configurator pages, where the decision happens.
- **Heritage is a material, not a filter.** Use the brand's own history (badges, colours, drawings) rather than a sepia grade.
- **High-consideration products earn depth.** A vehicle can carry a 3D look-around; a plate cannot. Match depth to price and doubt (`categories/ecommerce.md`).
- **Configurator paths stay plain.** The spec-and-buy steps are fast, keyboard-friendly and free of scroll tricks.

### What not to take
Immersion that slows the "add to basket" step. In this skill the purchase controls stay at Tier 1 motion.

<!-- file: references/teardowns/siena-film-foundation.md -->

## Teardown: Siena Film Foundation

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Day 18 Mar 2025 and Site of the Month Mar 2025 ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/organisation.md` · `styles/dark-luxe.md` · archetype `index`

### Structure
A black entry gate (wordmark, a ticket stub reading "admit one" with a ticket number, an Enter control), then an index of eight films as cards, then a thin credits footer.

### Type
A vintage high-contrast serif wordmark over a plain grotesk for everything else. Film titles are the only display type after the gate.

### Motion beats
1. The gate dismisses on Enter: the first interaction is buying a ticket.
2. Titles rise as masked lines.
3. Calls to action swap between two copies of the label and invert.
4. Dragging across a trailer scrubs it: the pointer is the playhead.

### What made it memorable
The metaphor (a cinema ticket) is the navigation, not decoration. Even the footer stays in the film lexicon.

### Principles to take
- **Let the first click be the concept.** An entry ritual is earned only when it says what the place is; otherwise it is a cookie wall.
- **Index archetypes need one strong row.** Eight items, one treatment, no exceptions. See `structures/` for the index archetype.
- **Give the pointer a job from the subject.** Scrubbing film with the pointer is the medium; a magnetic button would not be.
- **Two typefaces, strict roles.** A historical display face for the name, a quiet sans for the rest.

### What not to take
A gate that blocks content for search engines and for keyboard users. If you add a threshold, the content behind it must be in the HTML and the Enter control must be a real button.


---

<!-- file: references/teardowns/terminal-industries.md -->

## Teardown: Terminal Industries

**Award:** Awwwards Site of the Day 3 Sep 2025 and Site of the Month Sep 2025; CSSDA Website of the Day 4 Aug 2025 ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).
**Relevant to:** `categories/saas.md` · `styles/swiss.md` · archetype `console`

### Motion beats
Scroll turns 3D visuals into wireframe: the rendered object is stripped back to its structure as the visitor reads on ([observed teardown](https://github.com/coroboros/research/blob/main/articles/award-winning-websites-2025-2030/archetypes/immersive-cinematic.md)).

### What made it memorable
The transition is an argument: from the thing you see to the system underneath, which is what an infrastructure product sells.

### Principles to take
- **Use a transition to explain.** Render to wireframe says "here is how it works" without a diagram. Pick the transition whose meaning matches the next section.
- **Technical products can be beautiful without stock.** Show the system (`data/imagery.csv`, saas row: the product's own UI or structure, never stock).
- **One big transition, not ten.** A single meaningful state change is remembered; ten are noise.

### What not to take
Wireframe as decoration on a product that has no structure to show.

<!-- file: templates/CRITIQUE.md -->

## CRITIQUE.md · <project>

**Written after Checkpoint 5.** Fill this in at Checkpoint 6, from the `/critique` output on the design the author approved at Checkpoint 5 (Design review), never on a draft or a preview (`thinking/sequence.md` → Delivery flow). A gate failure is fixed and the design re-presented before this file is final.

The `/critique` output, pasted, never typed (`commands/critique-format.md`). Three sections, no mixing (`gates/delivery-gate.md`, "Every report"). A section with nothing in it says `none`.

### Measured

Only what a tool printed, with the tool named.

- gate.mjs: H <n> · M <n> · V <n> · Q <n> · A <n> · S <n> with traces · gate: … · rules: … · journey: …
- contrast.mjs: <failing pairs with ratios, or "0 failures">
- performance: <numbers a tool printed>
- originality.mjs: <scores against earlier builds, if it ran>

### Judged

Opinions, each marked `(opinion)` with who judged (`self`, or a named `judge`). Evidence is cited, not restated.

- self (opinion): C <n> · R <n> (counted from my own Restraint Gate record)
- self (opinion): Verdict: <one sentence>
- self (opinion): Top 3 problems, each with where, why it matters, evidence (`see Measured: …` or "by eye") and the fix
- self (opinion): AI-default scan by eye, Restraint Gate per questioned element, motion, choreography, keyboard by hand
- judge (opinion): <independent judge, named, or "none">
- self (opinion): Keep: <1–3 things> · Next command: <one>

### Not verified

- <each check that did not run or could not decide, with the reason>

<!-- file: templates/DATA.md -->

## DATA.md: <Project name>

> The shape of the `data/` folder: the committed mock data that lets the template run with zero configuration. Written with `SCHEMA.md`; every entity here is an entity in `SCHEMA.md` → Data model, with the same field names and types.

All data in data/ is demo. Replace with real data before launch.

<!--
Rules for the data/ folder
- One JSON file per entity: data/<entity-plural>.json (products.json, posts.json, settings.json). Derive the list from
  SCHEMA.md; there is no fixed set.
- Each file: { "demo": true, "entity": "<Entity>", "items": [ { ...fields, "demo": true } ] }. A single record
  (settings) is { "demo": true, "entity": "Settings", "item": { ... } }.
- Every entry carries "demo": true. scripts/completeness.mjs fails a data file whose entries are not labelled.
- The schema.json in data/ is a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) with one $defs entry per entity; each data file validates against it.
- Ids are stable strings; references use ids (ref(Entity) in SCHEMA.md).
- Images are local, under public/demo/, with width, height and alt in the entry. No hotlinked images.
- No real personal data: demo people use example.com addresses and +8800000000000-style placeholder numbers.
- Enough entries to show every state: at least one list long enough to paginate, one empty case reachable
  (a filter with no results), one item in each enum state (in stock / out of stock, draft / published).
- The code reads data/ through one typed module (lib/data.ts or equivalent). Swapping to a real source changes that
  module only.
-->

### Files

| File | Entity (`SCHEMA.md`) | Entries | Covers states |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/<entity-plural>.json` | <Entity> | <n> | <e.g. one out of stock, one on sale, enough for 2 pages> |
| the `schema.json` in `data/` | all, as `$defs` | — | — |

### Example entry

```json
{
  "demo": true,
  "entity": "<Entity>",
  "items": [
    { "id": "<id>", "<field>": "<value>", "demo": true }
  ]
}
```

### Loader

- **Module:** `<lib/data.ts>`: typed getters (`get<Entities>()`, `get<Entity>(id)`), the only place that reads `data/`.
- **Types:** generated from or written to match the `schema.json` in `data/`.
- **Switching to real data:** <what replaces the loader: CMS client, database query, API call>, and the environment variables it needs (all in `.env.example`).

### Replacing demo data

1. Replace each file's `items` with real entries; remove `"demo": true` from the file and every entry.
2. Validate against the `schema.json` in `data/`.
3. Remove the demo line from `README.md` only when no demo entry is left.

<!-- file: templates/GATE.md -->

## GATE.md · <project>

**Written after Checkpoint 5.** Fill this in at Checkpoint 6, from the gate output on the design the author approved at Checkpoint 5 (Design review), never on a draft or a preview (`thinking/sequence.md` → Delivery flow). A gate failure is fixed and the design re-presented before this file is final.

The first line is the status `node scripts/handoff.mjs <site>` printed, pasted (`gates/handoff.md`):

```
handoff: <VALIDATED | CONDITIONAL | NOT VALIDATED | REFERENCE> · <hash> · gate <date> · journey: …
```

Check this file against the record before the handoff push: `node scripts/handoff.mjs <site> --report GATE.md` (exit 2: the note claims more than the record; fix the note). Nothing below may claim more than that line: with any status but VALIDATED, no "fully validated", "all journeys work", "production-ready".

The gate output per page, pasted from `node scripts/gate.mjs …`, never typed. Three sections, no mixing (`gates/delivery-gate.md`, "Every report"). A section with nothing in it says `none`.

### Measured

What `scripts/gate.mjs` (and any other tool) printed, per page. Paste; do not summarise.

```
<page path or URL> · gate.mjs <version> · <date> · Chromium <version>
<the full output: gate: … · rules: … · the X lines · the J lines (nav, mobile, forms, loading, errors, session) · PASS/FAIL>
<the stamp line>
```

```
originality.mjs <this build> <earlier builds>   (axis O; only if it ran)
<the pair table it printed>
```

### Judged

Opinions, each marked `(opinion)` with who judged. The gate prints C and R, but it counts the agent's own Restraint Gate record, so they live here.

- self (opinion): C <n> · R <n>, from `DESIGN.md` → Restraint Gate record
- self (opinion): AI-default scan (`gates/delivery-gate.md` Part 2) answered by eye: <n>/25 failed, <numbers>
- self (opinion): craft checklist (Part 3) items checked by eye: <failed items or "none">
- judge (opinion): <independent judge, named, or "none">

### Not verified

Each check that did not run or could not decide, with the reason. No claim either way.

- <every exception handoff.mjs listed under "not verified", one per line (a CONDITIONAL note lists all of them)>
- <"gate.mjs: not verified — no browser" / "timed out after 600 s" / "the full gate did not run: development checks only (--rules, --journey)" / axes marked `?` and the missing record>
- <journey checks that printed `n/a`, and why: "forms: no form on any page">
- <O: not run, no earlier build to compare>
- <prototype boundaries handoff.mjs listed: forms saved only in this browser, labelled simulations, unavailable features>
- <real devices, screen readers, copy accuracy: not checked>

> The data contract. Written at the same time as DESIGN.md (not after the build), and shipped with every build as part of the template (`templates/TEMPLATE.md`). Every entity, every route, every state, the API surface and the handoff notes. A backend developer reading this file alone builds the backend without asking a question. Every field, route, section and endpoint the page uses is here; nothing on the page reads data that isn't.
